It no longer seeds itself from Date.now() + Math.random(); that stream was unreproducible and NOT provably fair, so an unseeded game looked identical to a fair one.

True Random Number Array Generator.name: True Random Number Array Generator

FAILS CLOSED: with no cryptographic RNG available the node REFUSES (throws, error in inspect data, Done still fires, array is emptied) — it never falls back to Math.random, which is not certifiable.

True Random Number Generator.name: True Random Number Generator

Wire value → ISAAC Random Number (Array) Generator.seed and Done → its Do. pixi.CellOverlay.name: pixi.CellOverlay
pixi.CellOverlay.shortDesc: Draws frames, glows, fills or sprites over reel-grid cells and multi-cell spans, on top of the reel columns.
pixi.CellOverlay.description: Draws highlights OVER reel-grid cells and multi-cell spans without touching the reel columns — the visual half of Sticky Symbols, Expand Symbols, Hold And Win Grid and Locked Reels. Place it in the SAME pixi.Container (or pixi.Stage) as the pixi.ReelColumn nodes, AFTER them in the tree so it renders on top (or turn on Sort Children by Z on that parent and give this node a higher zIndex). GEOMETRY MUST MATCH THE REELS: cellWidth / cellHeight / cellPadding / columnPadding are the PixiReelController values (its cellPadding is the ROW gap, columnPadding the COLUMN gap), and originX / originY are where column 0 and row 0 start inside that parent — with autoLayout on that is the controller's centring offset (read column 0's X and Y), with autoLayout off it is the first column's own x / y. A cell (row, col) covers x = originX + col * (cellWidth + columnPadding), y = originY + row * (cellHeight + cellPadding), size cellWidth x cellHeight; a span {row, col, rows, cols} covers rows x cols cells INCLUDING the gaps between them, anchored at its top-left cell. `cells` is an array of [row, col] pairs, 0-based, ROW FIRST (the Calculate Winnings / Cascade The Reels order); `spans` is an array of {row, col, rows, cols, symbol}. Styles: frame (a stroke of `thickness` px drawn INSIDE the cell edge, so it never spills onto a neighbour), glow (translucent bands bleeding outward from the cell, plus the frame), fill (a colour wash at `fillAlpha`, plus the frame; `fillAlpha` applies to this style only) and sprite (an image from `spriteImages`, keyed by symbol id — or by "default" for a plain cell — sized to the rectangle by `spriteFit`: contain letterboxes, cover crops to the rectangle). A span that carries a `symbol` draws its sprite under whichever style is active — that is how an expanding symbol is shown as one oversized image; a sprite whose URL is missing falls back to a frame and says so once in the console. Every redraw replaces everything drawn before it: set `cells` / `spans` per round, or fire `clear` (which also forgets the current cells and spans) and `redraw` (draws the current data again, e.g. after the layout changed). `pulse` breathes the whole overlay's alpha on the pixi ticker at `pulseSpeed` cycles per second; the ticker is released when pulse is off, nothing is drawn, or the node unmounts. IT DOES NOT HIDE OR FREEZE THE SYMBOL BENEATH IT: a fill or sprite covers the art only as far as its alpha allows, and the reel keeps spinning under a highlight — for a real lock the maths (Sticky Symbols / Hold And Win Grid) must keep the symbol in place and the reel controller must be told not to spin that column. Outputs: `container` (the PIXI.Container, for other pixi nodes), `drawnCount` (cells + spans drawn by the last redraw) and `onDrawn` (fires after every redraw, a clear included — read drawnCount to tell them apart).

pixi.Wheel.name: pixi.Wheel
pixi.Wheel.shortDesc: A segmented bonus wheel that spins to the segment the maths chose and stops with it under the pointer.
pixi.Wheel.description: The visual half of a wheel bonus: a segmented disc that spins to a segment the maths already chose. It decides NOTHING — wire Wheel Spin's `segmentIndex` (or any 0-based index) into `targetIndex`, then fire `spinTo`; the wheel turns clockwise for at least `extraTurns` whole turns over `durationMs` with the chosen `easing`, then snaps so the centre of segment `targetIndex` sits exactly under the pointer at 12 o'clock. Angle convention (shared with Wheel Spin): segment i spans [i, i + 1) * 360 / N degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock, its centre is at (i + 0.5) * 360 / N, and the pointer is fixed at 12 o'clock. `segments` is an array of strings or of {label, colour} objects (or a number N for N segments labelled 1..N); a segment without a colour takes the next entry of `colours`, cycled, or a built-in palette when `colours` is empty. Drawn with PIXI.Graphics and PIXI.Text, no GSAP; the spin runs on the pixi ticker and survives a hidden tab (PIXI clamps the frame delta, so a background spin simply takes longer). `spinTo` while already spinning restarts from the current angle toward the new target, and the abandoned spin fires no onSpinComplete. A `targetIndex` outside 0..N-1 is wrapped and warned about in the console — it means the maths and this wheel disagree on N; fix the segment list, not the index. Outputs: `container` (the root PIXI.Container, at x / y inside this node's pixi parent), `currentIndex` (the segment under the pointer once stopped; 0 at rest before any spin), `isSpinning`, `rotationDeg` (the disc's rotation, 0..360 clockwise, updated every frame — drive a tick sound or a light chase from it), `onSpinStart` and `onSpinComplete`. Fire the payout / next-step logic from `onSpinComplete`, never from Wheel Spin's own Done, or the win shows before the wheel has stopped.

Calculate Winnings.name: Calculate Winnings
Calculate Winnings.description: Turns Check Wins `winningLines` into MONEY. Wire `winningLines` AND `paylines` from the same Check Wins, `paytable` from Get Paytable, and keep `wildSymbol` identical to Check Wins `wildSymbol` (drift picks the wrong payout symbol). THE STAKE IS PER LINE, NOT PER SPIN: each line is worth `(betAmount / paylines.length) * paytable[symbol][runLength]`, where `symbol` is the first NON-wild symbol of the run and `runLength` is how many cells matched — so `paytable` must have an entry for that exact length or the line pays 0. ROUNDING IS A REAL TRAP: the per-line value is passed through `Math.round`, so ANY line worth less than 0.5 pays ZERO and is dropped from `winningLinesDetails` entirely (no payline highlight, no win, but the spin was still charged). With betAmount 1 over 20 paylines the per-line stake is 0.05, so every payout multiplier below 10 pays nothing at all. Measured 2026-09-08 over 200k simulated spins on stock weights and the stock Get Paytable formula "2.25 + 0.75 * x": at betAmount 1, 9-10% of paying lines round to zero and roughly 2-6% of winning spins pay exactly 0 (the spread is the strip layout and the seed; 4.1% on the fixed layout, 2.4% measured on another seed), and the round-UPs push RTP 5.5 points ABOVE its true value; on a low-multiplier paytable at betAmount 1 it is 100% of lines — the game charges every spin and never pays, which is what a 5x3 Olympus-style build did. At betAmount 100 the same games lose nothing to rounding. The rounding itself is UNCHANGED (moving it would move every existing game RTP): instead the node warns once on the console and reports `unroundedSpinWinnings`, `quantisationLoss`, `linesQuantisedToZero` and `betAmountPerLine` in its inspect data. Outputs: `spinWinnings` (number, already rounded) and `winningLinesDetails` ({line, symbols, positions, payout}, positions [row, col]).

Cascade The Reels.name: Cascade The Reels
Cascade The Reels.description: Tumble/cascade REMOVER + REFILL. It does NOT find wins and has no adjacency or cluster logic of its own: it clears ONLY the cells named in `winningLinesDetails`, drops the survivors down each column, refills the gaps from the top (weighted by `symbolWeights`, drawn from `Seeds` — REQUIRED: wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array → Seeds; unseeded it FAILS CLOSED: throws "[Cascade The Reels] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, empties `reels` and still fires Done — it no longer falls back to Math.random, which is not provably fair) and emits the new grid on `reels`. Fed no winningLinesDetails it clears NOTHING and still fires Done, so a silent no-op looks like a working cascade. `winningLinesDetails` shape: an array of objects, and only `positions` is read, as [row, col] pairs — ROW FIRST, the opposite order from Check Wins customPaylines ([col,row]) — e.g. [{ positions: [[2,0],[3,0],[2,1]], payout: 40 }]. {row, col} objects work too; out-of-range or other shapes are skipped in silence. Calculate Winnings:winningLinesDetails and Reel Ways Calculate Winnings:winningLinesDetails already emit this; Check Wins:winningLines does NOT (no positions), so wiring that in clears nothing. THE LOOP CONTRACT, and the part builds keep getting wrong: the grid is STATE. Hold it in a Variable2, wire that variable into `reels`, and write the `reels` output of this node BACK to the same variable each pass (Cascade.reels -> SetVariable -> Variable2 -> Cascade.reels). Wiring Weighted Reels:reels straight into `reels` gives a cascade that re-runs the original spin on every beat and never progresses. The WIN EVALUATOR and the DISPLAY must both read that same variable, or the maths scores a grid the player never saw. FIRING: one Do per evaluation pass, after the winningLinesDetails for that pass have been computed; the chain ends on the pass that pays nothing.

Check Wins.name: Check Wins
Check Wins.description: Scores FIXED PAYLINES on a spun grid. Reads `reels` as columns-of-rows (reels[col][row]) and, for each payline, walks the cells that line names looking for `minConsecutiveSymbols`+ of the same symbol from the LEFT, with `wildSymbol` matching anything. `wildSymbol` (default 9) and `freeSpinsSymbol` (default 10) MUST BE DIFFERENT SYMBOLS: when they are equal, every payline whose FIRST cell is that symbol is SKIPPED and pays nothing — the wild-led lines, the ones that pay most (2026-09-08: a 5x3 build set freeSpinsSymbol 9, left wildSymbol at its default 9, and paid zero across twenty live spins while the reels looked right). The node now warns once on the console and reports `wildScatterCollision` plus `linesDroppedByFreeSpinsInterference` in its inspect data; if the game has no scatter, point `freeSpinsSymbol` at a symbol index the reels never produce. With `customPaylines` unwired it uses a BUILT-IN table of twenty 5-long lines across COLUMNS 0-4 on ROWS 0-2 ONLY — on any grid that is not 5x3 it scores just those 15 cells and silently ignores every other cell (a 7x7 grid: 15 of 49). `customPaylines` is Array<Array<[col,row]>> and can express any fixed SHAPE (V, zigzag, a hand-listed lattice), but a payline is an ORDERED list of cells, so this node has NO notion of a connected same-symbol group. IT DOES NOT DO CLUSTER PAYS, adjacency, flood fill, or scatter-anywhere pays — there is no such code in this file and no other node in the library evaluates them either; write that in a JS function. Output `winningLines` is [[lineNumber, [symbols...]], ...] and carries NO CELL POSITIONS, so it cannot be wired into Cascade The Reels:winningLinesDetails (which needs positions and would clear nothing) — positions come from Calculate Winnings:winningLinesDetails. FIRING: Weighted Reels.Done -> Do, with the same grid on `reels`; scoring is deferred to after inputs settle, and it fires Done even on error (with empty winningLines).

Accessibility Settings.name: Accessibility Settings
Accessibility Settings.description: Reads accessibility preferences and turns them into values you multiply and switch on: `motionScale` is 1 normally and `motionScaleWhenReduced` (default 0.25) when reduced motion is active, so multiply spin, cascade and celebration durations by it; `reducedMotion` is the boolean behind it (`auto` follows the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting live, `on`/`off` force it). `highContrast` and `colourBlindMode` are passed through for your own switches, and `palette` is an object { mode, colours: [six hex], c0..c5 } of six distinguishable colours for the selected mode (Okabe-Ito for `none`, red-green-safe sets for deuteranopia/protanopia, a blue-yellow-safe set for tritanopia; a design aid, not a certification). `changed` fires whenever any output changes, including an OS setting flip, so wire it to whatever re-applies durations and tints; `refresh` re-reads the OS setting on demand.

Audio Mixer.name: Audio Mixer
Audio Mixer.description: Central volume bus for a game (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). Wire `musicVolume`, `sfxVolume` and `voiceVolume` into the volume input of your Sound nodes; each equals `master` x that channel level x the duck factor, and is 0 while `muted`. Fire `duck` to pull every channel down to `duckLevel` over `duckMs` (for a big-win voice-over or a dialog) and `unduck` to restore; `duckActive` reports the state. Any other change (master, muted, a channel level) ramps over `fadeMs` (0 = immediate). The most recent change decides the ramp time; a new change restarts the ramp from the current values. `changed` fires on every value update, including each ramp frame, so it can kick a Sound node that only re-reads its volume on a signal. Ramps use requestAnimationFrame in the browser (a timer elsewhere) and are cancelled when the node is deleted.

Autoplay.name: Autoplay
Autoplay.description: Client-side autoplay controller for a slot UI (not compiled to the RGS). Wire `spin` to the same input your Spin button drives (it fires once per auto round), the reel controller Done/onAllStopped or Reel Stop Watcher.allStopped to `roundComplete`, the round win to `lastWin`, the player balance to `balance`, a free-spins/bonus flag to `featureTriggered`, and Jurisdiction Rules.autoplayAllowed to `allowed`. `start` arms `spins` rounds, sets `active`/`remaining` and fires `spin` immediately; when `allowed` is false it instead fires `stopped` with `stopReason` "not-allowed". Each `roundComplete` increments `spinsDone`, decrements `remaining` and checks the stop conditions in this order: feature (`stopOnFeature` and `featureTriggered`), win (`stopOnAnyWin` with `lastWin` > 0, or `lastWin` above `stopOnWinAbove`; 0 = off), balance (`balance` below `stopOnBalanceBelow`; 0 = off), count (`remaining` reached 0). If none applies the next `spin` fires after `delayMs`. `stop` ends the run with "manual". `stopped` fires once per run with the reason in `stopReason`; `active` goes false. Reset `featureTriggered` and `lastWin` upstream each round or the condition re-triggers. `start` while `active` is ignored; stop first. The delay timer is cleared on stop and when the node is deleted.

Bet Mode.name: Bet Mode
Bet Mode.description: Ante bet / bonus buy stake maths (compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). `mode` is "base" (default), "ante" (stake x `anteMultiplier`, default 1.25) or "bonus_buy" ("bonusbuy", "feature_buy" and "buy" also work; stake x `bonusBuyMultiplier`, default 100), or any key of `customMultipliers` ({ mode: multiplier }); unknown modes fall back to base with `modeKnown` false. With `direction` base-to-cost (default) `betAmount` is the base bet and `cost` = betAmount x multiplier (deduct this from the balance); with cost-to-base `betAmount` is what the player pays and `baseBet` = betAmount / multiplier. On `Do`: `mode` (normalised), `modeKnown`, `multiplier`, `cost`, `baseBet`, `stakeForPaytable` (= baseBet — wire it to Calculate Winnings.betAmount so the paytable pays on the base stake), `isBase`, `isAnte`, `isBonusBuy` and `forceFeature` (true for a bonus buy — read it after Done to force the free-spin trigger; booleans, not signals). Money is integer minor units and the results are rounded.

Chapter Branch.name: Chapter Branch
Chapter Branch.description: A story / chapter state machine for narrative slots and multi-stage bonus games (matrix row F25). `chapters` is an object keyed by chapter id, e.g. { "intro": { "next": "forest", "paytableScale": 1 }, "forest": { "next": { "left": "cave", "right": "river" } }, "cave": { "next": ["river", "intro"] }, "river": {} }. `next` may be a string (one path), an object (choose by key) or an array (choose by value or by 0-based index; an array of one needs no choice); a chapter without `next` is an end. Every other field in a chapter is yours — reel strips, symbol weights, paytable scale, background id — and comes back verbatim on `chapter`, ready for Variant Selector.variants or Paytable Modifier. STATEFUL: `Do` emits the current chapter (starting at `startKey`, else the first key of `chapters`); set `choice` and fire `advance` to move along the matching path (a choice that resolves to no chapter stays put and reports `changed` false); `reset` returns to `startKey`. Outputs: `chapter` (the current chapter object), `currentKey`, `nextKeys` (the paths available now), `isEnd` (no paths left), `changed` (this call moved) and `chapterIndex` (the position of the current key in `chapters`, -1 when unknown). STATE PERSISTENCE: kept in the node between calls in the editor; on the RGS the state persists across rounds only for identified players (ctx.state) — guest sessions replay stateless, so a guest restarts at `startKey` every round. Seedless and deterministic; branching by chance belongs in Feature Trigger or Wheel Spin, feeding `choice`. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores.

Cluster Pays.name: Cluster Pays
Cluster Pays.description: Pays clusters of adjacent matching symbols instead of paylines (compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). Wire `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels (columns of rows, 1-based symbols, 0 = blank), `paytable` from Get Paytable.paytable ({ symbol: { size: multiplier } } — the largest size key <= the cluster size pays) and `betAmount` from the bet. A cluster is every group of at least `minClusterSize` cells of one symbol connected by `adjacency` (orthogonal = 4-way, diagonal = 8-way); `wildSymbol` cells (0 = none) join any cluster and count toward its size when `wildsCountTowardSize` is true. On `Do`: `clusters` = [{ symbol, size, cells, wilds, positions [row, col], multiplier, payout }], `winningLinesDetails` in the Calculate Winnings shape ({ line, symbols, positions, payout }) — wire it to Cascade The Reels / Directional Cascade.winningLinesDetails so the paid cells are removed, `clusterWinnings` = the total in minor units (betAmount x multiplier per cluster, rounded; the whole bet, not bet / paylines), `clusterCount`, `hasWin` (a boolean, not a signal) and `largestCluster`. On a bad grid the node logs the error, writes it to inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done.

Coin Collector.name: Coin Collector
Coin Collector.description: Collects the coin values on the grid when a collector symbol lands (Cash Collect; compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). Wire `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels (or the Sticky Symbols / Hold And Win Grid output grid) and `valueGrid` from Symbol Value Grid.valueGrid. `collectorSymbol` is the symbol that collects (0 = none); with `requireCollector` true (default) nothing is paid unless at least one collector landed, and with `multiplyByCollectors` the total is multiplied by the number of collectors. On `Do`: `collected` (minor units — add it to the round win, e.g. into Calculate Winnings.totalWin downstream), `totalOnGrid`, `coinPositions` and `coinCount` (wire to pixi.CellOverlay.cells or a fly-to-collector animation), `collectorPositions`, `collectorCount`, `hasCollector` and `paid` (booleans, not signals). On a bad grid the node logs the error, writes it to inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done.

Column Spin Router.name: Column Spin Router
Column Spin Router.description: Spins only the free columns of a reel grid so hold-and-win respins, locked reels and sticky rounds leave the other columns untouched (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). pixi.ReelController always spins every column it owns, so wire the columns to this node instead: spin0…spin11 → each pixi.ReelColumn.spin, stop0…stop11 → .stop, target0…target11 → .targetSymbols and stopPos0…stopPos11 → .stopPosition. Set `freeColumns` to the indices that may spin (Locked Reels / Hold And Win Grid give you this list; empty = every column below `columnCount`) and fire `spin`: spinN fires for the free columns only and `lockedColumns` lists the rest. When the result is in, set `targetSymbols` (the full grid reels[col][row]) and `stopPositions`, then fire `stop`: every free column gets its own column of symbols on targetN and its stop index on stopPosN before stopN fires (the values land first, so the column has its data when it stops), while locked columns receive nothing and keep their symbols. `stop` uses the free set of the last `spin`. `routed` fires after each spin and each stop. Pair it with Reel Stop Watcher (arm it before `spin`, same `expected` columns) to learn when the free columns have all stopped.

Directional Cascade.name: Directional Cascade
Directional Cascade.description: Tumble / cascade REMOVER + REFILL with a gravity direction (matrix rows F21 and B5). It does NOT find wins: it clears ONLY the cells named in `winningLinesDetails` — wire Calculate Winnings.winningLinesDetails, Reel Ways Calculate Winnings.winningLinesDetails or Cluster Pays.winningLinesDetails; only `positions` is read, as [row, col] pairs, ROW FIRST — slides the survivors toward `direction` and refills the gaps from the opposite edge with symbols weighted by `symbolWeights` (the Weighted Reels weights; the symbols already on the grid when empty), drawn from `Seeds`. down = survivors fall, refill enters from the top (the classic tumble, and EXACTLY what Cascade The Reels does: same reels, winningLinesDetails, symbolWeights and Seeds give the same grid); up = survivors rise, refill from the bottom; left / right = survivors slide along each row, refill from the right / left edge. `Seeds` is REQUIRED whenever something clears: wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array -> Seeds (a fresh array per pass, or every cascade refills alike). Unseeded it FAILS CLOSED: throws "[Directional Cascade] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done. With nothing to clear the grid passes through unchanged, `hadRemoval` is false and no seed is consumed. Outputs: `reels` (the new grid, columns-of-rows), `removedPositions` ([row, col], deduplicated, out-of-range skipped), `removedCount`, `hadRemoval` (wire to Multiplier Ladder.step so the tumble multiplier climbs once per cascade that removed something, and to the Condition that decides whether to score again) and `direction` (the direction applied). THE LOOP CONTRACT (the same as Cascade The Reels): the grid is STATE — hold it in a Variable2, wire that variable into `reels`, write the `reels` output BACK to the same variable each pass, and let the win evaluator and the display read that same variable; wiring Weighted Reels.reels straight in re-cascades the original spin on every beat and the tumble never progresses. Fire `Do` once per evaluation pass, after that pass has been scored; the chain ends on the pass that pays nothing. Stateless. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores.

Expand Symbols.name: Expand Symbols
Expand Symbols.description: Expands every landed `symbol` into a `mode` shape on the grid and emits the rewritten grid on `reels`: column (the whole reel — the classic expanding wild), row, cross (row + column), block2x2 / block3x3 (a square anchored at the symbol, clamped to the grid) or cell (only the anchor cell, useful together with `replaceWith`). Written cells take `replaceWith` when it is set, else the symbol itself; `minCount` is how many anchors must land before anything expands (fewer = the grid passes through unchanged, `changed` false). Wire `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels, or from the Variable2 that holds the evolving grid. Outputs: `reels` (columns-of-rows, the same shape as the input), `spans` ({row, col, rows, cols, symbol} rectangles — wire to pixi.CellOverlay.spans to draw one oversized symbol over the expanded area), `anchors` ([row, col] pairs of the symbols that triggered the expansion, ROW FIRST), `expandedCount` (cells that changed) and `changed`. THE LOOP CONTRACT (the same as Cascade The Reels): the grid is STATE — hold it in a Variable2, wire that variable into `reels`, write the `reels` output of this node BACK to the same variable, and let the win evaluator (Calculate Winnings / Cluster Pays) and the display read that same variable, or the maths scores a grid the player never saw. Fire `Do` once per evaluation pass, after the spin has landed and before the win evaluator runs. Stateless and seedless: the same inputs always give the same grid, so there is no `Seeds` port. Fails closed on a malformed grid (empty or ragged `reels`): the error is logged as "[Expand Symbols] ...", written into inspect data, every output is emptied and Done still fires. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the editor preview and the server produce the same grid.

Feature Trigger.name: Feature Trigger
Feature Trigger.description: A seeded probability roll: `triggered` is true with probability `chance` (0..1, clamped) — the generic random trigger behind mystery features, random wilds, bonus-wheel entries and "feature drops" (matrix row E19). Deterministic and auditable: `roll` is the first Park-Miller LCG float seeded from Seeds[0] (the same generator Weighted Reels uses) and `triggered` = roll < chance, so the same seed always gives the same answer. `Seeds` is REQUIRED: wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array -> Seeds — and use a DIFFERENT ISAAC array (or at least a different element) from the one that spun the reels, or the trigger correlates with the spin outcome. Unseeded it FAILS CLOSED: throws "[Feature Trigger] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, sets `triggered` false, `roll` 0 and `chance` 0, and still fires Done — it never falls back to Math.random, which is not provably fair. Fire `Do` once per round after the seeds are in; wire `triggered` into a Condition (or Switch) node to branch the round, e.g. into Wheel Spin, Pick Bonus or Symbol Upgrade.activate. `chance` echoes the clamped probability used. Stateless. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the server rolls exactly what the preview rolled from the same seed.

Hold And Win Grid.name: Hold And Win Grid
Hold And Win Grid.description: Hold-and-win / coin respin bonus at cell granularity (matrix row F20): coins lock in place with a value each, every other cell respins, a new coin resets the respin counter, and the bonus ends when the counter hits 0 or the grid is full. STATEFUL and SEEDED. Fire `start` with the triggering spin in `reels` (Weighted Reels.reels): every cell showing `coinSymbol` locks and gets a value — taken from `valueGrid` when a Symbol Value Grid already priced that cell, else drawn from `coinValues` weighted by `coinValueWeights` (bet multiples of `betAmount`, integer minor units, when `valuesAreBetMultiples` is true; face values otherwise). Then fire `respin` once per respin: the node itself redraws every unlocked cell from `symbolWeights` (the Weighted Reels weights; the symbols already on the grid when empty) and locks any new coin, so no external spin is needed — the maths owns the respin, the reels only animate it. `Do` with no flag re-emits the current state (and behaves like `start` while idle); `reset` clears. `Seeds` is REQUIRED for every draw: wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array -> Seeds (a fresh array per call, or the respins repeat). Unseeded it FAILS CLOSED: throws "[Hold And Win Grid] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done. Outputs: `grid` (coins in place, `blankSymbol` everywhere else — the grid to display and to score), `valueGrid` (the coin value per cell, same columns-of-rows shape), `lockedCells` ([row, col] pairs, ROW FIRST — wire to pixi.CellOverlay.cells to frame the held coins), `lockedCount`, `newCoins` (locked by this call), `respinsLeft`, `isComplete` (true on the call that ends the bonus — pay `totalValue` then), `active`, `totalValue` (the sum of every held coin) and `isFull`. THE LOOP CONTRACT (the same as Cascade The Reels): the grid is STATE — hold it in a Variable2, wire that variable into `reels`, write the `grid` output BACK to the same variable, and let the display and any win evaluator read that same variable, or the player sees a grid the maths never scored. STATE PERSISTENCE: kept in the node between calls in the editor; on the RGS the state persists across rounds only for identified players (ctx.state) — guest sessions replay stateless, so a multi-request hold-and-win needs an identified player. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the same seeds give the same coins on both sides.

Jackpot Tiers.name: Jackpot Tiers
Jackpot Tiers.description: Fixed local jackpots awarded by symbol count (Mini / Minor / Major; compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). Wire `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels and `betAmount` from the bet. `tiers` is an array of { name, count, multiplier } (an optional `fixed` = a flat award in minor units instead of betAmount x multiplier); the highest tier whose `count` the grid reaches wins. On `Do`: `symbolCount` and `positions` ([row, col]) of `jackpotSymbol` (wire the positions to pixi.CellOverlay.cells), `tierIndex` (-1 when no tier is reached), `tierName`, `multiplier`, `award` (minor units — add it to the round win) and `hasTier` (a boolean, not a signal — wire it to RGS Jackpot Pools.shouldClaim when the top tier should claim a progressive pool). This node is for fixed, bet-multiple jackpots; the progressive pools of the platform are read and claimed through RGS Jackpot Pools. On a bad grid the node logs the error, writes it to inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done.

Jurisdiction Rules.name: Jurisdiction Rules
Jurisdiction Rules.description: Resolves the per-jurisdiction UX rules a slot must obey and exposes them as booleans/numbers you gate your UI with: hide the Autoplay button when `autoplayAllowed` is false, cap the bet picker at `maxStake`, feed `realityCheckIntervalMin` into Reality Check and `minSpinIntervalMs` into your spin-button cooldown. Priority: a non-empty `rules` object (the `jurisdiction` shape of the XRGS `__client-rules` route, or that whole response) wins and fires `loaded` with `source` = "input"; otherwise wire GameInit → `fetch` with `gameSlug` (+ optional `rgsUrl`) to GET `{rgsUrl}/rgs-fn/{gameSlug}/__client-rules` with no auth headers and get `source` = "server"; until either happens the fallback* inputs apply with `source` = "default". `maxStake` 0 means unlimited; `minSpinIntervalMs` / `realityCheckIntervalMin` 0 mean no rule. A failed fetch keeps the fallbacks, writes `error` and fires `failed`, so the game keeps running on the safe defaults you chose.

Locked Reels.name: Locked Reels
Locked Reels.description: Reel-level lock and respin (locked reels / respin features, matrix rows E16 and F20 at column granularity): a column that shows `lockSymbol` (or is listed in `lockColumns`, 0-based) is frozen and its landed symbols are kept while the other columns respin. STATEFUL. Fire `start` with the triggering spin in `reels` (Weighted Reels.reels): every column holding `lockSymbol` locks, `respinsLeft` becomes `respins` and `active` turns true. Then, for each respin, spin ONLY the free columns — wire `freeColumns` -> Column Spin Router.freeColumns so the reel controller spins just those — feed the new grid into `reels` and fire `Do`: locked columns are restored from the frozen copy, any free column that now shows `lockSymbol` locks too (`newLocks`), and `respinsLeft` goes back to `respins` when something new locked (with `resetOnNewLock` true) or counts down by one otherwise. `roundOver` turns true on the call where `respinsLeft` reaches 0 or every column is locked; `reset` clears everything. `Do` while inactive behaves like `start` (locks whatever shows `lockSymbol`, activating only if a column locked). Outputs: `reels` (the merged grid — the one the display must show and the win evaluator must score), `lockedColumns` / `freeColumns` (0-based column indices), `lockedCount`, `newLocks`, `respinsLeft`, `roundOver`, `active`. THE LOOP CONTRACT (the same as Cascade The Reels): the grid is STATE — hold it in a Variable2, wire that variable into `reels`, write the `reels` output BACK to the same variable, and let the win evaluator (Calculate Winnings / Cluster Pays) and the display read that same variable, or the maths scores a grid the player never saw. STATE PERSISTENCE: kept in the node between calls in the editor; on the RGS the state persists across rounds only for identified players (ctx.state) — guest sessions replay stateless, so a guest gets a single-round lock. Fails closed on a malformed grid (empty or ragged `reels`): the error is logged as "[Locked Reels] ...", written into inspect data, every output is emptied (the state is left untouched) and Done still fires. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores.

Multiplier Ladder.name: Multiplier Ladder
Multiplier Ladder.description: A win multiplier that climbs a ladder (cascade / tumble multipliers, free-spin multiplier ladders; compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). `ladder` is the list of multipliers (default [1, 2, 3, 5]) and the meter starts at `startIndex`. Fire `step` (from Cascade The Reels.Done, Cluster Pays.hasWin ...) to move `stepBy` rungs (negative steps down; clamped to the ladder), or set `stepOnDo` true to step on every `Do`. `reset` returns to `startIndex` — fire it at the start of a new spin so a cascade multiplier restarts. Outputs after each evaluation: `multiplier` (multiply the win with it, or wire it to the Calculate Winnings stake), `index`, `atMax`, `changed` (booleans, not signals) and the parsed `ladder`. Each `step`/`reset` signal is its own evaluation on the client, so use either `step` or `stepOnDo`, not both in one spin. State (the index) lives in the node; on the RGS it persists across rounds only for identified players — guest sessions replay stateless.

Paytable Modifier.name: Paytable Modifier
Paytable Modifier.description: Rewrites a paytable ({ symbol: { count: multiplier } }, the Get Paytable / Calculate Winnings shape) for a bet mode, a bonus round, a chapter or a variant (matrix row F24). mode scale: every multiplier is multiplied by `scale`, then by the per-symbol factor in `symbolOverrides` ({ "7": 2 } doubles symbol 7 only). mode absolute: `symbolOverrides` holds whole rows ({ "7": { "3": 50, "5": 500 } }) whose counts replace the originals outright (counts not listed still get `scale`; a bare number in absolute mode acts as a factor). Every result is rounded to `roundTo` decimals. Wire `paytable` from Get Paytable.paytable (or Variant Selector.paytable / Chapter Branch.chapter data) and the `paytable` output into Calculate Winnings.paytable — and into Paytable Rows.paytable, so the rows the player sees are the rows that pay. Outputs: `paytable` (the rewritten table, same shape), `changed` (true when any multiplier differs from the input) and `scale` (the factor applied). Fire `Do` when the bet mode, chapter or feature changes; stateless and seedless, so the same inputs always give the same table. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the server pays from the same rows the preview showed.

Paytable Rows.name: Paytable Rows
Paytable Rows.description: Turns a paytable ({ symbol: { count: multiplier } }, the Get Paytable shape) into display rows for the pay table / info screen (matrix row G30), priced at the current bet: payout = round(betAmount / paylinesCount x multiplier), the Calculate Winnings convention in integer minor units. `symbolNames` maps symbol ids to names — an array (index = symbol - 1) or an object keyed by symbol id; unnamed symbols show their number. Wire `paytable` from Get Paytable.paytable (or from Paytable Modifier.paytable, so the screen shows the multipliers that are actually paying), `betAmount` from the bet control and `paylinesCount` from the payline definition. Outputs: `rows` ([{ symbol, name, entries: [{ count, multiplier, payout }] }], symbols ascending, counts ascending — one row per symbol, ready for a Repeater), `flatRows` (one entry per symbol-count pair: { symbol, name, count, multiplier, payout }, for a flat list or table), `symbolCount` and `betPerLine`. Re-fire `Do` whenever the bet changes so the payouts refresh; stateless and seedless. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the numbers the player reads are the numbers the server pays.

Performance Budget.name: Performance Budget
Performance Budget.description: Watches the frame rate, JS heap and page load time of the running game against budgets and tells you when to degrade (fewer particles, no blur, static backgrounds) (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). Fire `start` (GameInit) and every `sampleMs` it publishes `fps` (frames counted with requestAnimationFrame over the window), `heapMB` (performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize, Chromium only, 0 where unavailable) and `loadTimeMs` (navigation timing, 0 until the load event has finished), sets `overBudget` and `report` ({ fps, heapMB, loadTimeMs, breaches: ["fps" | "heap" | "load"] }) and fires `sampled`. `budgetExceeded` fires once per breach type when `fps` drops below `fpsBudget`, `heapMB` rises above `heapBudgetMB` or `loadTimeMs` exceeds `loadTimeBudgetMs`, and fires again for that type only after it has recovered and breached anew, so wire it straight to your quality-downgrade logic and read `report.breaches` for the reason; a budget of 0 disables that check. `stop` pauses sampling and keeps the last values; `start` again resets the breach memory. Timers and the frame loop are cleared on stop and when the node is deleted.

Pick Bonus.name: Pick Bonus
Pick Bonus.description: Pick-and-reveal bonus (matrix row F23): a hidden pool made of `prizes` plus `endMarkers` copies of `endValue`, shuffled ONCE from `Seeds`, then revealed one tile at a time. STATEFUL and SEEDED. Fire `start` to build and shuffle the pool — `Seeds` is REQUIRED here: wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array -> Seeds; unseeded it FAILS CLOSED (throws "[Pick Bonus] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done). Then, per tap, set `pickIndex` (0-based, the tile the player chose) and fire `pick`: the prize at that index is revealed and added to `total` — unless it is `endValue`, which ends the bonus (`lastIsEnd` true). `picks` > 0 caps the number of picks (0 = until an end marker or the pool is exhausted). `Do` re-emits the current state without changing it; `reset` clears everything. Set `pickIndex` and fire `pick` from the same tap in the same frame — the node waits for both to land. An already-revealed or out-of-range index is ignored (`revealedNow` false). Outputs: `revealed` ([{ index, prize }] revealed so far, in pick order — drive the tile faces from it), `total` (numeric prizes summed), `remaining` (picks left, -1 when uncapped), `ended`, `active`, `lastPrize` (what this pick showed, null when nothing was revealed), `lastIsEnd`, `revealedNow`, `poolSize`, `picksMade` and `hiddenCount`. Prizes may be numbers (added to `total`) or strings such as "FREE_SPINS" (revealed, counted, not summed); `endValue` is matched exactly. STATE PERSISTENCE: kept in the node between calls in the editor; on the RGS the state persists across rounds only for identified players (ctx.state) — guest sessions replay stateless, so a pick bonus spread over several requests needs an identified player. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the same seed shuffles the same pool on both sides.

Player Progress.name: Player Progress
Player Progress.description: Meta-progression for a slot: XP, levels and achievement unlocks kept as a small object you persist yourself. `addXp` adds `xp` to `totalXp`; `levelThresholds` is the cumulative XP needed to REACH each level (default [100,250,500,1000,2000] gives level 2 at 100 XP, level 6 at 2000, max level = thresholds + 1). Outputs: `level` (1-based), `totalXp`, `xpIntoLevel`, `xpToNext` (0 at max level), `progress` 0..1 for a bar, `achievements` (array of ids), `levelUp` (fires once per addXp that gains a level), `unlocked` (fires when `unlock` adds a NEW `achievementId`; repeats are ignored), `changed` after every mutation. Persistence: wire `stateOut` ({ totalXp, achievements }) into SaveGameSession.sessionData, and LoadGameSession.sessionData → `stateIn` then fire `load` (a JSON string is accepted too; an empty stateIn is ignored); `reset` clears everything. Pure client state that the server does not verify, so never pay money out of it.

Progressive Meter.name: Progressive Meter
Progressive Meter.description: A persistent fill meter that charges up across spins and fires a feature when full (compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). Every `Do` adds `increment` while `addOnDo` is true (default) — leave `add` unwired then; set `addOnDo` false and fire `add` (from Cluster Pays.hasWin, a scatter count, Coin Collector.paid ...) to charge only on demand. `setValue` (leave empty for none) overwrites the value before the add, `reset` returns to `startValue`. When `value` reaches `target`, `filled` is true for that evaluation and `fillCount` grows; with `resetOnFill` (default) the value wraps to `startValue`, plus the overflow when `carryOverflow` is true. Outputs after each evaluation: `value`, `progress` (0..1 — wire to a progress bar), `filled` (a boolean, not a signal — read it after Done to start the feature), `fillCount` and `remaining`. Each `add`/`reset` signal is its own evaluation on the client, so firing `add` and `Do` with `addOnDo` true in one spin adds twice in the editor while the server adds once — use one or the other. State (value, fillCount) lives in the node; on the RGS it persists across rounds only for identified players — guest sessions replay stateless.

Reality Check.name: Reality Check
Reality Check.description: Responsible-gaming reality check (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). Fire `start` when the play session begins: `sessionSeconds` and `elapsedMinutes` (whole minutes played) count up every second and `due` fires once `intervalMinutes` have elapsed. Show your reality-check dialog on `due` and fire `acknowledge` when the player dismisses it; that starts the next interval, and nothing re-fires until it is acknowledged. On every round set `bet` then fire `betPlaced`, and set `win` then fire `winPaid`, so `totalBet`, `totalWin` and `netPosition` (totalWin - totalBet) are right for the dialog copy; `checksShown` counts the checks. `stop` pauses the clock and keeps the totals for a session summary; `start` again resets everything. `intervalMinutes` 0 disables the check. Amounts are in whatever unit you feed in (the platform uses integer minor units). The 1-second timer is cleared on stop and when the node is deleted.

Reel Stop Watcher.name: Reel Stop Watcher
Reel Stop Watcher.description: Rebuilds the "all reels stopped" event for reel columns that are driven directly (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). pixi.ReelController.onAllStopped is armed only when that controller spins, so when Column Spin Router or your own logic fires pixi.ReelColumn.spin/stop per column nothing tells the game the round has settled: wire each column.onStopped into stopped0…stopped11, fire `arm` before the spins go out, and `allStopped` fires once every expected column has reported. `expected` is a comma list of column indices to wait for (e.g. "1,3" for the free columns of a hold-and-win respin; wire Column Spin Router.freeColumns through a Join or type it); leave it blank to wait for every column below `columnCount`. `stoppedCount` and `stoppedColumns` (in stop order) update as columns report, `armed` is true while watching, and a column that never reports trips the `timeoutMs` watchdog: `timedOut` fires and the watcher disarms (set the timeout above your longest spin plus anticipation). `disarm` cancels a watch; each `arm` clears the seen set, so the signals are re-triggerable every round. Column stops that arrive while not armed are ignored.

RGS Jackpot Pools.name: RGS Jackpot Pools
RGS Jackpot Pools.description: Reads the progressive jackpot pools of the published game and claims one (compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). On the server the platform injects the live pools from ctx.jackpots, so `mockPools`, `fetch`, `gameSlug` and `rgsUrl` are editor-only and never reach the server: set `mockPools` ([{ id, name, pool_type, current_value, claimable }]) for a preview, or set `gameSlug` (the slug of the published game) and fire `fetch` to GET {rgsUrl}/rgs-fn/{gameSlug}/__jackpots (the public read route; `rgsUrl` defaults to the production functions URL) — the fetched pools are stored and evaluated at once, and every later `Do` uses them instead of `mockPools`. `Do` outputs `pools` (normalised), `poolNames`, `poolCount`, `poolValues` ({ name: current_value } — wire it to the jackpot ticker) and `totalPoolValue`; `poolName` (name or id) selects one pool for `poolValue`, `poolFound` and `claimable`. With `shouldClaim` true (wire Jackpot Tiers.hasTier or a scatter-count comparison) the selected pool is claimed when it is claimable — or always, when `claimOnlyIfClaimable` is false: `claims` = [name], `claimed` = true. WIRE `claims` TO A Component Outputs PORT NAMED `jackpotClaims` so it reaches the platform as data.jackpot_claims — the RGS pays and resets the pool, this node does not move money. Only scatter-type pools are claimable; guests are ineligible, their claims are ignored. On a failed fetch (no fetch in this runtime, empty gameSlug, HTTP error) the node logs the error, writes it to inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done.

RGS Leaderboard.name: RGS Leaderboard
RGS Leaderboard.description: Reads the public tournament leaderboard for a game from XRGS: `fetch` GETs `{rgsUrl}/rgs-fn/{gameSlug}/__leaderboard` (add `tournamentId` to target one tournament, default = the current one) with no auth headers and outputs `entries` ([{ rank, display_name, score, prize_amount }] truncated to `limit`, 0 = all), `tournament` ({ id, name, status, starts_at, ends_at, scoring_metric } or null), `totalPlayers` and `hasTournament`; `loaded` fires after each successful read, `failed` + `error` on a network/HTTP error (the last good entries are kept). Set `pollMs` > 0 to refetch on an interval after `fetch` (the interval restarts on every `fetch`, follows a changed `pollMs`, and `stopPolling` or deleting the node clears it). Wire GameInit → fetch, entries → a Repeater/list for the ladder, hasTournament → the visibility of the tournament panel.

RGS Translations.name: RGS Translations
RGS Translations.description: Loads the XRGS translation catalogue for a game so the strings players see come from the platform, not from text typed into nodes (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). Set `gameSlug` and `lang` (a BCP-47 tag such as en, pt-BR, de) and fire `fetch`: the node GETs `{rgsUrl}/game-translations?lang=…&game_slug=…`, which returns the global chrome strings merged with that game's overrides along a fallback chain (pt-BR → pt → en), and publishes `strings` (an object of key → text), `lang` (the language actually served), `requestedLang`, `fallback` (true when a fallback language was served) and fires `loaded`; a network or HTTP failure fires `failed` with `error` and leaves the last good catalogue in place. `text` is the one string for `key` — change `key` any time and `text` follows, falling back to the key itself when it is missing, so a Text node wired to it never goes blank. Fire `listLanguages` to fill `languages` (every language the platform has strings for) for a language picker. Pair it with Languages Dictionary when the game also carries its own phrases, or wire `strings` into a JavaScript Function that formats {name}-style placeholders.

Screen Reader Announce.name: Screen Reader Announce
Screen Reader Announce.description: Speaks a message to screen-reader users without any visible UI: on `announce` it writes `text` into a visually hidden aria-live region it creates once in document.body (politeness "polite" = role status, waits for the reader to pause; "assertive" = role alert, interrupts, so use it for balance and limit warnings only). Repeating the same text is re-announced (the region is blanked and re-set a tick later), and the region is cleared after `clearAfterMs` (0 = leave it). Wire Win Rollup → announce with a formatted "You won 12.50" string, Reality Check → announce with assertive politeness, Reel Stop Watcher.allStopped → announce the result. `lastAnnouncement`, `announcedCount` and the `announced` signal update even when no DOM is present, so a chain wired after it keeps running.

Session Limits.name: Session Limits
Session Limits.description: Client-side session, loss and wager limits for UI and pre-checks (not compiled to the RGS). The platform enforces its own wager and loss limits server-side (rg_check_bet on XRGS runs on every bet); this node is the client-side counterpart that lets the UI warn and block before a bet is sent, so never rely on it alone. Fire `start` when play begins (it starts the session clock and zeroes the counters); on every round set `bet` then fire `betPlaced`, and set `win` then fire `winPaid`. `maxSessionMinutes`, `maxLoss` (bets minus wins) and `maxWager` (total bets) are each off at 0. When a limit is hit `limitReached` fires once, `limitType` says which ("session", "loss" or "wager", checked in that order) and `blocked` stays true until `reset`, which clears it and starts a fresh session with zeroed counters (wire it to the dialog dismiss). `remainingMinutes`, `remainingLoss` and `remainingWager` update live for the UI and are -1 while that limit is off. Loss and wager limits count without `start`; the session limit needs it. The 1-second timer is cleared when the node is deleted.

Sticky Symbols.name: Sticky Symbols
Sticky Symbols.description: Keeps landed symbols in place for the following spins (sticky wilds, sticky respins; compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). Wire the input `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels and put this node between the reels and the win evaluation: the output `reels` is the landed grid with the remembered stickies merged back in — wire it to Calculate Winnings / Cluster Pays.reels and to the reel visual. Every `Do` merges the stickies, ages them by one spin when `tick` is true (default) and, while `captureOnDo` is true (default), captures every `stickySymbol` cell the spin landed; set `captureOnDo` false and fire `capture` to capture only on demand (e.g. only inside free spins). `duration` = the number of spins a sticky survives (0 = until `reset`); `replaceWith` (empty = keep the symbol) shows another symbol in the sticky cells. Outputs: `stickyPositions` ([row, col] — wire to pixi.CellOverlay.cells for the sticky frames), `stickyCount` and `changed` (a boolean, not a signal). `reset` clears the stickies — fire it when the feature ends. Each `capture`/`reset` signal is its own evaluation on the client (it also merges and ages), so use either `capture` or `captureOnDo` in a spin, not both. State (the sticky cells) lives in the node; on the RGS it persists across rounds only for identified players — guest sessions replay stateless. On a bad grid the node logs the error, writes it to inspect data, empties every output (the stickies are kept) and still fires Done.

Symbol Upgrade.name: Symbol Upgrade
Symbol Upgrade.description: Swaps every `fromSymbol` on the grid for `toSymbol` while an upgrade is active (symbol upgrade / transform features, matrix row E18) and emits the rewritten grid on `reels`. STATEFUL. Fire `activate` to start an upgrade that lasts `duration` calls (0 = until `reset`); every `Do` then applies the swap to the incoming grid and counts one call off `remaining`. `reset` ends it. The activation rule is the same one the server applies: activate = (`activate` fired this call) OR (`activateOnDo` is true) — so with `activateOnDo` on, every `Do` re-arms the upgrade for `duration` calls and the swap never lapses. Wire `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels, or from the Variable2 that holds the evolving grid. Outputs: `reels` (columns-of-rows, the same shape as the input), `active`, `remaining` (calls left, -1 = until reset), `upgradedCount` (cells swapped by this call) and `changed`. THE LOOP CONTRACT (the same as Cascade The Reels): the grid is STATE — hold it in a Variable2, wire that variable into `reels`, write the `reels` output BACK to the same variable, and let the win evaluator (Calculate Winnings / Cluster Pays) and the display read that same variable, or the maths scores a grid the player never saw. STATE PERSISTENCE: kept in the node between calls in the editor; on the RGS the state persists across rounds only for identified players (ctx.state) — guest sessions replay stateless, so a multi-spin upgrade lasts one round for guests. Fails closed on a malformed grid (empty or ragged `reels`): the error is logged as "[Symbol Upgrade] ...", written into inspect data, every output is emptied (the state is left untouched) and Done still fires. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores.

Symbol Value Grid.name: Symbol Value Grid
Symbol Value Grid.description: Gives every `valueSymbol` cell on the grid a coin value (money symbols / Cash Collect maths; compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). Wire `reels` from Weighted Reels.reels and `Seeds` from ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array (one seed is enough — the draw uses the same Park-Miller generator as Weighted Reels, so the preview and the server land the same values). `values` are the possible coin values and `weights` their draw weights (same length; empty = uniform); with `valuesAreBetMultiples` true (default) each value is multiplied by `betAmount` and rounded to minor units. On `Do`: `valueGrid` (same shape as reels, 0 where there is no coin), `coinPositions` ([row, col]), `coinCount` and `totalValue`. Wire `valueGrid` to Coin Collector.valueGrid (and to Hold And Win Grid.valueGrid) and `coinPositions` to pixi.CellOverlay.cells or a value-label layer. FAILS CLOSED: with coins on the grid and no seeds the node logs "[Symbol Value Grid] Seeds is required", writes it to inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done — unseeded outcomes are not provably fair and are refused.

Telemetry Event.name: Telemetry Event
Telemetry Event.description: Client-side analytics queue for a slot (not compiled to the RGS, never on the money path). Set `event` (a name such as "spin", "feature_enter", "autoplay_stop") and an optional `payload` object of extra fields, then fire `send`: the event is stamped with `ts` (ms epoch) and `sessionId` and queued. `sessionId` is generated once (random hex) when the input is empty; set it to reuse a server session id. With `batch` true the queue is POSTed as JSON `{ events: [{ event, payload, ts, sessionId }] }` to `endpoint` when it reaches `maxBatch` events, when `flushMs` has elapsed since the first queued event, or on `flush`; with `batch` false every event posts at once. `headers` is merged over Content-Type: application/json (put your API key here). Requests use fetch with keepalive so a flush during navigation completes, and on pagehide (tab closing or navigating away) whatever is still queued goes out with navigator.sendBeacon. `queued`, `sent` and `failed` count events; `flushed` fires after each accepted POST and `sendFailed` (with `error`) after a rejected or non-2xx one, whose batch is dropped rather than retried. An empty `event` or `endpoint` counts as a failure so a miswire is visible in the counters. Wire your spin / feature / win nodes into `send`, GameInit → `flush` on exit paths, and leave the defaults otherwise.

Variant Selector.name: Variant Selector
Variant Selector.description: Picks one maths variant (an RTP set, a market or a regional build) out of a `variants` object ({ key: { reelStrips, symbolWeights, paytable, paytableScale, rtp, ... } }; compiles to the RGS; the editor and the server run the same slot-feature-cores maths). `key` selects the variant (wire it from Jurisdiction Rules, a Bet Mode output or a config value), `fallbackKey` is used when that key is missing, and with an empty key the first variant is used. On `Do`: `variant` (the whole object), `selectedKey`, `found` (a boolean, not a signal), `keys`, plus the common fields unpacked for wiring — `reelStrips` (to Weighted Reels.reelStrips), `symbolWeights` (to Weighted Reels / Cascade The Reels.symbolWeights), `paytable` (to Calculate Winnings.paytable or Paytable Modifier.paytable), `paytableScale` (to Paytable Modifier.scale) and `rtp` (for the info screen). Fields the variant does not carry come out empty: [] / {}, scale 1, rtp 0.

Volume Ramp.name: Volume Ramp
Volume Ramp.description: Tweens a number from `from` to `to` over `durationMs` with the chosen `easing` (client-side, frame driven, not compiled to the RGS). `start` (re)starts the ramp: `value` snaps to `from`, `progress` to 0, `running` becomes true and `tick` fires; every frame then updates `value` and `progress` (0..1) and fires `tick`; the final frame sets `value` = `to`, `progress` = 1, `running` = false, fires `tick` and then `finished`. `stop` freezes `value` where it is and clears `running` without firing `finished`. `durationMs` 0 jumps straight to the end. Wire `value` into a Sound node volume, a sprite alpha or any number input; two ramps started by the same signal (one 1 to 0, one 0 to 1) make a crossfade. Frames use requestAnimationFrame in the browser and a timer elsewhere, and are cancelled when the node is deleted.

Wheel Spin.name: Wheel Spin
Wheel Spin.description: The maths half of a bonus wheel (matrix row F22): picks ONE segment by weight from `Seeds` and reports it; the wheel graphic then merely spins to it. `segments` is an array of labels (strings or numbers) or of { label, weight, prize } objects; `weights` and `prizes` are optional parallel arrays that override per index (a segment with no weight anywhere weighs 1; a bare numeric segment doubles as its own prize when `prizes` is empty). `Seeds` is REQUIRED: wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array -> Seeds. Unseeded it FAILS CLOSED: throws "[Wheel Spin] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, empties every output and still fires Done; an empty segment list or all-zero weights fail the same way. Outputs: `segmentIndex` (0-based — wire to pixi.Wheel.targetIndex and then fire its spinTo; pay and continue from pixi.Wheel.onSpinComplete, NOT from this Done, or the win shows before the wheel has stopped), `prize` (the raw prize of the chosen segment, number or string as given), `prizeValue` (the prize as a number, 0 when it is not numeric), `label`, `angle` (the centre of the segment in degrees clockwise from the top — segment i spans [i, i + 1) x 360 / N, the convention pixi.Wheel shares), `sweep` (360 / segmentCount), `segmentCount` and `segments` (the normalised { label, weight, prize } list, handy for drawing the disc). Fire `Do` once per wheel award, after the seeds are in. Stateless. Compiles to the RGS through the shared slot-feature cores, so the server lands the same segment from the same seed.

Wide Grid Bridge.name: Wide Grid Bridge
Wide Grid Bridge.description: Runs a reel grid wider than 12 columns on two pixi.ReelController nodes and makes them behave as one (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). A controller owns at most 12 columns, so the grid is split at `splitAt` (default 12): controller A gets columns 0…splitAt-1, controller B the rest. Wire the full maths grid (reels[col][row]) into `spinResult`; `spinResultA` / `spinResultB` update the moment it changes, so wire them into each controller.spinResult. Wire your Spin button into `spin` and `spinA` / `spinB` into each controller.spin (spinB is skipped when the last grid did not reach past splitAt). Wire each controller.onAllStopped into `allStoppedA` / `allStoppedB`: `allStopped` fires once, after both halves have reported for the latest spin, so wire it where a single controller.onAllStopped used to go (Calculate Winnings, Win Rollup, Autoplay.roundComplete). `currentSymbolsA` / `currentSymbolsB` (each controller.currentSymbols) are concatenated into `currentSymbols`, the full grid for Check Jackpot / cell overlays, and `columnCount` is the total width. Set `spinResult` before, or in the same update as, `spin` so both halves have their data when they start.

Win Rollup.name: Win Rollup
Win Rollup.description: Counts a win up on screen (client-side, not compiled to the RGS). Set `amount` (Calculate Winnings.totalWin) and fire `start`: `value` rolls from 0 to the amount over `durationMs` and `text` is rebuilt every frame; `skip` jumps to the end (wire a tap on the win banner). With `minorUnits` true (the platform convention: amounts are integer cents) `value` and `text` show `amount` / 100; set it false for amounts already in display units. `text` = `prefix` + value fixed to `decimals` + `suffix`, ready for a Text node. `tick` fires when the roll starts, every `tickEveryMs` while rolling and once more at the end, so wire it to the play input of a coin/rollup Sound node; `finished` fires when the final value is shown (immediately when `amount` is 0 or `durationMs` is 0). `running` is true while rolling. Each `start` restarts from 0. Frames use requestAnimationFrame in the browser and a timer elsewhere, and are cancelled when the node is deleted.

Reel Ways Calculate Winnings.name: Reel Ways Calculate Winnings
Reel Ways Calculate Winnings.description: Turns Reel Ways Check Wins `winningLines` into MONEY. Wire `winningLines` from Reel Ways Check Wins (NOT from Check Wins — different shape: each entry here is [[symbols...], [[row, col], ...]]), `paytable` from Get Paytable, and keep `wildSymbol` identical to Reel Ways Check Wins `wildSymbol` (drift picks the wrong payout symbol). THE STAKE IS THE WHOLE betAmount PER WAY, not per line: each way pays `Math.round(betAmount * paytable[symbol][wayLength])`, where `symbol` is the first NON-wild symbol of the way and `wayLength` is how many reels it spans — so `paytable` needs an entry for that exact length or the way pays 0, and a way made entirely of wilds pays 0. ROUNDING IS PER WAY: the value is passed through `Math.round`, so ANY way worth less than 0.5 pays ZERO and is dropped from `winningLinesDetails` entirely (no highlight, no win, but the spin was still charged); at a small betAmount with fractional multipliers that can be every way on the screen — the game charges every spin and never pays. Because ways multiply (a screen full of one symbol is many entries), the rounding error compounds across them. The rounding itself is unchanged (moving it would move every existing ways game RTP). Outputs: `spinWinnings` (number, already rounded, summed over every way) and `winningLinesDetails` ({symbols, positions, payout}, positions [row, col]).

Reel Ways Check Wins.name: Reel Ways Check Wins
Reel Ways Check Wins.description: Scores WAYS wins (243-ways style: any position on adjacent reels, LEFT to RIGHT) on a spun grid. Reads `reels` as columns-of-rows (reels[col][row]); a way is a same-symbol run of at least `minConsecutiveSymbols` reels starting at reel 0, with `wildSymbol` matching anything. `wildSymbol` (default 9) and `freeSpinsSymbol` (default 10) MUST BE DIFFERENT SYMBOLS — the same trap as Check Wins (2026-09-08: a 5x3 build set freeSpinsSymbol to the wild index and paid nothing). Here the collision is quieter but still wrong: the scatter is removed from the candidate symbol set (`symbolSet.delete(freeSpinsSymbol)`), so when the two are one symbol it is the WILD that is silently deleted — a way made entirely of wilds is never scored, and the symbol plays both roles at once. The node warns once on the console and reports `wildScatterCollision` in its inspect data; if the game has no scatter, point `freeSpinsSymbol` at an index the reels never produce. Symbols are 1-based and `numberOfSymbols` bounds the candidate set (1..numberOfSymbols), so a wild or scatter index ABOVE numberOfSymbols is simply never a paying symbol, which is the intended layout. Output `winningLines` is [[[symbols...], [[row, col], ...]], ...] — one entry PER WAY (a cartesian product across reels, so a screen full of one symbol produces many entries), each with its cell positions; feed it to Reel Ways Calculate Winnings, not to Calculate Winnings (different shape). FIRING: Weighted Reels.Done -> Do, same grid on `reels`; fires Done even on error (with empty winningLines).

SlotMainEngine.name: SlotMainEngine
SlotMainEngine.description: DEPRECATED — simulation/prototype only. SlotMainEngine is a monolithic engine (strips, spin, wins, cascades, free spins and jackpot in one node) that is NOT RGS-extractable. It is SEEDED and FAILS CLOSED: wire True Random Number Generator.value → seed (or ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array → Seeds); with neither wired, Generate Reel Strips and Spin REFUSE (console error + inspect text, no Done) instead of drawing from Math.random. It fires Done after every spin. For any production or RGS slot, use the decomposed provably-fair pipeline instead: True Random Number Generator -> ISAAC -> Generate Symbol Weights -> Reel Strips Generator -> Get Paytable -> Weighted Reels -> Check Wins -> Calculate Winnings -> Spin Calculate -> Spin Result.

Spin Calculate.name: Spin Calculate
Spin Calculate.description: Per-spin bank: takes the previous capital / totalBets / totalWinnings / spinCount / hits, applies this spin and emits the new values. CASCADING CHANGES WHO PAYS FOR THE SPIN — read this before wiring a tumble game. Internally: isCascadingInProgress = cascadingReelsEnabled AND spinWinnings > 0, and the bet deduction, the hits increment and the spinCount increment are ALL skipped while that is true. So with cascadingReelsEnabled true the bet is charged ONLY on a call where spinWinnings reads 0. Two rules follow and breaking either makes the game FREE TO PLAY at full payout: (1) `spinWinnings` must be the win of THIS evaluation pass — wire Calculate Winnings:spinWinnings (or the per-pass payout of your own evaluator) directly. NEVER wire a running total or an accumulator Variable2: at settle an accumulated total is greater than zero on every winning spin, the node reads that as "a cascade is still in progress", and no bet is ever deducted. (2) It must FIRE on the pass that pays NOTHING — that zero-winnings call is the only one that charges the bet and advances spinCount. Triggering it only from the win branch of a Condition, or only from the settle branch while its winnings input still holds the chain total, means the charge call never happens. With cascadingReelsEnabled false the node bills once per Do, which is what a non-cascading slot wants. Also note `hits` is unreachable while cascadingReelsEnabled is true (the increment requires spinWinnings > 0 and NOT isCascadingInProgress, which cannot both hold) — count hit rate outside this node. FIRING: Calculate Winnings.Done -> Do, then Done -> Spin Result.Do.

Weighted Reels.name: Weighted Reels
Weighted Reels.description: Turns reel strips + seeds into the landed grid (`reels`, columns-of-rows) and `stopPosList`. `Seeds` is REQUIRED in every mode that draws (static without an input stopPosList, dynamic, and both free-spin paths): wire ISAAC Random Number Array Generator.array → Seeds, one seed per column (size >= number of reels). FAILS CLOSED: unseeded, the node REFUSES — it throws "[Weighted Reels] Seeds is required", logs it, writes the error into inspect data, empties `reels`/`stopPosList` and still fires Done. It no longer falls back to Math.random (dynamic paths did until 2026-09-08); an unseeded spin is not provably fair and looked identical to a fair one.
